summary: The prepared main source already contains the issue's performance-preserving solution: Engine creates one independent MultiprocessingSerializer payload per TP rank and TPWorker deserializes only the payload indexed by its rank. A new regression uses real CPU tensor storage handles and four spawned consumers; all ranks succeed. The original serialize-once payload still reproduces one success and seven EOFError failures, confirming the test targets the reported defect.

tests.what_was_measured: Issue-specific legacy topology with one ForkingPickler tensor payload shared by eight spawned consumers: one restored 1048576 bf16 elements and seven raised EOFError; the resource_sharer logged seven KeyError failures. Raw output: reports/j-3461c967711b/evidence/legacy_one_payload.txt

Three tests passed: four independently serialized CPU tensor payloads were consumed concurrently by four spawned TP-rank stand-ins; TP1 retained one valid multiprocessing payload; raw and base64 pre-serialized flattened_bucket inputs normalized without reserialization. Raw output: reports/j-3461c967711b/evidence/regression_test.txt

gpu_execution_evidence: The defect and regression concern CPU tensor ForkingPickler/resource_sharer file-descriptor ownership. No GPU operation was relevant or used.
remaining_limitations: Only one gfx950 GPU was assigned, so the reported TP8 server topology could not be reproduced.
No model weights were used; this does not validate LoRA semantic accuracy, Qwen3 behavior, HTTP transport, or a full scheduler/model-worker lifecycle.
The evidence qualifies the per-rank serialization/deserialization mechanism with real spawned processes, not a multi-node workload.
